name: hip pain overview
title: Hip pain sorted by where the patient points: anterior or groin pain inside the joint (hip osteoarthritis, labral tear), lateral pain (greater trochanter bursitis and greater trochanteric pain syndrome) and posterior buttock pain (piriformis syndrome), each with its presentation, exam, investigations and treatment in order, plus the socks question that separates lateral hip osteoarthritis from greater trochanteric pain syndrome

root.title: 'My hip hurts': ask WHERE
lines: TRUE hip pain (inside the joint) is usually ANTERIOR, in the GROIN
patients often point to the lateral buttock, sometimes to the buttock itself

groups.title: ANTERIOR / GROIN: usually inside the joint
lines: also: rheumatoid or septic arthritis · osteonecrosis · iliopsoas tendinopathy

groups.title: LATERAL
lines: hip OA can present here too: ask about SOCKS

head: h
Hip osteoarthritis (OA)
primary: idiopathic, elderly · secondary: post-traumatic, younger
clue: t
Groin pain, the 'C' sign
• worse with prolonged activity · night pain
• morning stiffness < 30 min · stiff after long sitting
• crepitus, locking · TROUBLE PUTTING SOCKS ON
inv: • X-ray confirms it, and changes may not match symptoms
• CT or MRI not needed (secondary causes, surgical planning)
tx: • image-guided injection: steroid, hyaluronic acid or platelet-rich plasma

head: h
Labral tear
all ages · commonly ACTIVE FEMALES
clue: t
Vague groin pain
• CLICKING, catching, snapping
• locking
inv: • X-ray only to exclude other causes

head: h
Greater trochanter bursitis
very common · female > male
friction of the iliotibial band over the trochanter irritates the bursa
clue: t
Pain over the greater trochanter
• CAN'T LIE ON THAT SIDE · worse weight bearing
• ± to the buttock or down the thigh to the knee
• NO swelling, redness or skin change
inv: • ask about a recent increase in activity
tx: stretch the iliotibial band, strengthen the hip abductors

head: h
Greater trochanteric pain syndrome (GTPS)
chronic tendinopathy of gluteus medius + minimus, which insert on the trochanter
bursitis is only half the story
clue: t
Looks like bursitis, but MORE CHRONIC and recalcitrant
• insidious and slowly worse, OR a sudden flare after unaccustomed exercise, a fall, prolonged weight bearing, sporting overuse
• chronic tendinosis with acute flares of bursitis or tendinitis
tx: stretch the iliotibial band, STRENGTHEN the hip abductors

head: h
Piriformis syndrome
muscle strain or tendinopathy ± SCIATIC nerve impingement
clue: t
Buttock pain
• worse getting out of bed, sitting long, moving the hip
• radicular symptoms down the leg if the nerve is caught
• after buttock trauma, long sitting, anatomic anomalies
inv: only if the nerve is involved
tx: stretch piriformis · range of motion · deep massage

panels.title: Lateral pain: bursitis / GTPS or hip OA?
items: bursitis / GTPS: pain on activity and lying on it · tender trochanter · GTPS: single leg stance hurts
hip OA: morning stiffness, groin pain, progressive · socks hard · internal + external rotation painful

panels.title: Tests and the rest
items: FABER = flexion, abduction, external rotation · FADIR or FAIR = flexion, adduction, internal rotation
osteonecrosis: trauma, steroids, alcohol, lupus, sickle cell, radiation
snapping hip: very common · not painful → don't worry about it
